sections.title: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means
Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder

defenses.argument: The prosecution has failed to establish the specific intention or knowledge required for Attempt to Murder under Section 109, as the act was done with the intention of causing grievous hurt (perforated intestine) rather than death. The facts state the accused stabbed the complainant in a fit of quarrel over a parking space; there is no evidence he intended to kill or knew that his act would cause death. defenses.argument: The prosecution has not adduced evidence to prove that the accused voluntarily caused 'grievous hurt' as defined in Section 116. While the medical report records a perforated intestine, which falls under clause (h) of Section 116 ('hurt which endangers life'), the facts do not explicitly state that the injury was inflicted with the specific intent to cause grievous hurt or by means specifically enumerated in Section 118(1). The charge relies on an inference that the nature of the wound automatically constitutes 'grievous hurt' without addressing the subjective element of voluntary causation of
defenses.fact_quote: Surgeons repaired a perforated intestine, and the medical report records the injury as dangerous to life.

defenses.argument: The charge of Culpable Homicide not amounting to Murder under Section 105 is legally unsustainable because the offence of culpable homicide, by definition, requires a death or an act done with the intention of causing death. The Reviewer's doubt correctly identifies that this section presupposes a death has occurred, whereas the facts only report grievous hurt and no mention of death. Since the complainant survived and there is no evidence of death, the essential ingredient of 'culpable homicide' (an act likely to cause death or done with intent to cause death) cannot be established.
